title: Ventilator Classification & Modes of Ventilation Quiz

questions.text: A patient's compliance suddenly decreases while being ventilated in volume-control mode. What change would you expect to see?

answers.text: Peak inspiratory pressure increases; tidal volume remains constant
Tidal volume decreases; peak pressure remains constant
Both tidal volume and peak pressure decrease
No change — the ventilator adjusts both automatically

questions.text: In pressure-control mode, a patient develops new-onset bronchospasm. What would you expect?

answers.text: Tidal volume decreases; inspiratory pressure remains constant
Peak pressure increases; tidal volume remains constant
Both tidal volume and pressure increase equally
Expiratory time shortens and auto-PEEP develops
Trigger
Target
Cycle
Baseline

questions.text: Pressure Support Ventilation (PSV) is classified as which breath type?

answers.text: Supported — patient triggered, pressure targeted, flow cycled
Mandatory — ventilator triggered, pressure targeted, ventilator cycled
Assisted — patient triggered, volume targeted, ventilator cycled
Spontaneous — patient triggered, baseline targeted, patient cycled

questions.text: In Assist/Control (A/C) mode, the patient triggers extra breaths beyond the set rate. What happens to those extra breaths?

answers.text: They are fully supported by the ventilator and cycled by the ventilator
They are unsupported — the patient does all the work for extra breaths
Extra breaths are blocked until the next mandatory cycle
They are pressure-supported but patient cycled

questions.text: Which mode is specifically indicated for refractory hypoxemia in ARDS and uses an inverse I:E ratio with two pressure levels?

answers.text: APRV — Airway Pressure Release Ventilation
SIMV + PS
PSV at high support levels
CMV in pressure-control mode

questions.text: What is the primary advantage of SIMV over CMV for a patient who is beginning to recover respiratory muscle function?

answers.text: SIMV allows spontaneous breaths between mandatory breaths, exercising respiratory muscles
SIMV guarantees a higher tidal volume with each breath
SIMV eliminates the risk of auto-PEEP
SIMV uses pressure control exclusively to reduce barotrauma

questions.text: What is the control variable, and how many control variables can a ventilator use simultaneously?

answers.text: The primary variable the ventilator controls during inspiration; only one at a time
The variable that triggers inspiration; multiple can be used simultaneously
The variable that cycles the breath to exhalation; one or two depending on mode
The baseline pressure maintained during exhalation; one per breath type

questions.text: An ICU ventilator is described as a combination-powered device. What does this mean?

answers.text: It requires both a 50 psi gas source and an electrical power source to operate
It can switch between pressure and volume control automatically
It uses both pneumatic and fluidic control circuits
It delivers a combination of mandatory and spontaneous breaths simultaneously

questions.text: In Pressure Support Ventilation, what signals the ventilator to cycle into exhalation?

answers.text: Inspiratory flow decelerates to 25% of peak inspiratory flow
A preset tidal volume has been delivered
A preset inspiratory time has elapsed
Peak inspiratory pressure reaches the set support level
